title: Grothendieck infinity-groupoids and the homotopy hypothesis
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: Henry's pushout conjecture for every Grothendieck coherator, after OpenAI's 2026 proof: freely adjoining to a cellular infinity-groupoid a cell parallel to a given one and a cell joining the two is a weak equivalence. Globular theories, coherators and their models (complete, cocomplete, with free objects and the small object argument); the homotopy calculus of division and exact boundaries; coskeletal cutoffs, spines and contractible free shapes; trees and whiskers; partial cylinders and the descending induction; the canonical left semi-model structure, and the Quillen equivalence with spaces from Henry's comparison theorem.
prerequisites: basic category theory: presheaves, the Yoneda lemma (course Schemes, The functor of points and representability, Theorem 1.1) and left Kan extensions (course Derivators, Kan extensions and the derivator axioms, Theorem 2.1)
test categories and Grothendieck's homotopy programme (course AG-AS), for context

open_obligations: H Henry's comparison theorem (Henry, Algebraic models of homotopy types and the homotopy hypothesis, arXiv:1609.04622, Theorem 5.1.2(5) with Propositions 5.3.6, 5.3.7, Lemmas 5.3.9, 5.3.11 and Corollaries 5.3.12, 5.3.13): if every elementary expansion of a finitely cellular model is a weak equivalence, the finitely cellular models form a cylinder coherator whose completion is Mod(C) with its canonical semi-model structure, and the fundamental infinity-groupoid functor from spaces is a right Quillen equivalence. Used in lesson 6, Section 3 (Corollary 3.1). Intended home: a course on cylinder categories and their completions.
The Quillen model structure on topological spaces is part of the statement of H and is not proved in the programme.
